citations.narrative:
Some enclosures lacked public barriers, thereby allowing public contact with animals. The facility representative conveyed
an attendant isn't always present in these areas to observe public interaction with these animals:
- In the pastures at the top of the hill, 2 ostriches, 6 emus, 1 zebra, 1 barbary sheep, 1 goat, 3 llamas, 2 alpacas, 2 cows,
1 zebu, and 1 Watusi were in front of the fence or laying by the fence where the public could touch and feed them.
- Enclosures housing sixteen rabbits and three pigs were able to be touched and fed by the public. The lack of a barrier
doesn't prevent possible contact if the animals go to the front of the enclosure.
The lack of a public barrier that allows contact with animals does not minimize risk of harm to the animals or to the public.
Ensure that there is an adequate barrier and/or distance between the animals and general viewing public so as to assure
the safety of animals and the public. Correct by: August 19, 2026

Sixteen adult rabbits were housed in a primary enclosure that allowed access to 6 chickens, 10 turkeys, and 4 guineafowl
that were free roaming in the building. The avian species were able to eat and lay down alongside the rabbits. The rabbits
appeared to be in good condition, and while the enclosure provided sufficient space, shelter, and access to food and
water, rabbits are a species that are not permitted to be co-housed with any other species, unless for specific scientific
purposes. Housing rabbits with other species may result in injury or compatibility issues. Correct by ensuring rabbits shall
not be housed in the same primary enclosure with any other species of animals. Correct by: August 19, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Rebecca Nanney, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
